claims.text: Selective oxidation kinetics of the X element govern formation and persistence of the protective oxide on CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C.
A suitable concentration and distribution of X promotes formation of a continuous, epitaxially aligned oxide.
Si is especially effective among Si, Mn, and Al at promoting the proposed protective oxide.
The continuous, epitaxially aligned oxide accommodates thermal and mechanical stresses.
The proposed oxide limits further oxide growth.
Stress accommodation and limited oxide growth prevent cracking and spallation under high-temperature oxidative or corrosive conditions.
Selective oxidation of X produces an oxide with slower growth kinetics than oxides associated with the other alloying elements.
The X-derived oxide has a lower diffusion rate than oxides associated with the other elements.
The X-derived oxide forms a coherent interface with the CrFeCoNiX substrate.
A coherent oxide–substrate interface reduces thermal-mismatch stresses.
The coherent interface impedes crack initiation and propagation.
CrFeCoNiX alloys with an optimal and homogeneous X distribution will form a slow-growing, adherent oxide that remains free of cracking and spallation during the specified exposure.
CrFeCoNiX alloys lacking the effective X concentration or distribution will show less stable oxide behavior.
Previously studied CrMoTiAlY alloys have documented unstable oxide scales.
Variations in X content critically influence oxidation behavior in single- or multiphase CrFeCoNiX metallic solid solutions above 900 °C.
